perf.summary: Replace 64-bit modulo in Fisher-Yates with Lemire multiply-shift bounded reduction.
perf.currentCost: Line 37 does seed % (ulong)(i+1) every iteration: a full 64-bit unsigned integer division (~20-40+ cycles, not pipelined) per shuffle step.
perf.proposedChange: Use j=(int)(((seed>>32)*(ulong)(i+1))>>32) (Lemire-style: multiply the high 32 random bits by the range and take the high word). Replaces div with one 64-bit multiply + shift.
perf.rationale: A widening multiply + shift is ~3-5 cycles and fully pipelined versus a non-pipelined 64-bit division, on the hot O(n) shuffle path that runs on every Welzl call.
perf.risk: Changes the exact permutation produced from the fixed seed (different but still valid uniform-ish shuffle). Welzl is correct for ANY permutation, so output circle is unaffected; only the (non-contractual) randomization order changes. If a test pins the exact shuffle sequence, keep modulo.

perf.summary: Inline the DistSq computation to avoid recomputing center deltas.
perf.currentCost: Line 44 computes cx,cy then calls DistSq(x1,y1,cx,cy), which recomputes (x1-cx) and (y1-cy). Since cx=(x1+x2)/2, x1-cx equals (x1-x2)/2 and is the half-delta already implied.
perf.proposedChange: double hx=(x1-x2)*0.5, hy=(y1-y2)*0.5; cx=x1-hx... or simply R=Math.Sqrt(hx*hx+hy*hy). Avoids the DistSq call and its duplicate subtractions.
perf.rationale: Removes one helper call and 2 redundant subtractions on a hot leaf used in the inner Welzl loops; reuses deltas that define the midpoint.
perf.risk: Floating-point result differs by at most last ULP from current (x1-cx) form due to reassociation; values otherwise identical. If bit-exact reproduction of current R is required, keep DistSq form.

perf.summary: Add AggressiveInlining to the leaf-ish Solve3/Solve2 only if small; otherwise leave and instead mark Welzl entry without inlining.
perf.currentCost: Welzl, Solve2, Solve3 carry no inlining hints. These are not tiny, so forced inlining is not warranted; current state is acceptable.
perf.proposedChange: No change recommended to inlining of Solve2/Solve3 (they are loop bodies, too large to inline). Documented here only to flag that the existing absence of attributes is correct and should NOT be 'fixed' by adding AggressiveInlining.
perf.rationale: Prevents a cargo-cult regression: inlining the Solve methods would bloat call sites with no win. Leaving them out-of-line is optimal.
perf.risk: None; this is a no-op recommendation guarding against an incorrect change.
